clue.text: Odd fetes I'd skip for an arts competition

indicators.note: to skip is to caper about, so the letters of the preceding words jump into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone avoids an odd assortment of fêtes in favour of an arts contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skip' reads as 'miss out', but it is the anagram signal working on ODD FETES I'D. An EISTEDDFOD is a Welsh festival of music and poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh festival is a competitive gathering of poets, singers and musicians.

clue.text: Asian listener grasps name of English novelist

indicators.note: something that grasps holds another thing within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a listener is an ear, the organ of hearing
Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: An Asian reader takes hold of an English novelist's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the East, especially Asia, is called by this noun.

clue.text: Second, more generous recording of representative items

parts.note: ampler means fuller or more generous

explanation.surface: A second, fuller album collects typical tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampler is an album collecting typical tracks as a taster of a range.

clue.text: Old man holding up info on the Spanish land-tax

indicators.note: a container holding something keeps it inside, so these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: dad, one's old man, is one's father

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A father holds up details of a Spanish tax on land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives NEG; GEN is British slang for information, a usage solvers abroad may not know, and the tax was paid to Viking raiders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon levy raised to pay off Viking raiders was assessed on land holdings.

clue.text: In desert, read out-of-date paper to recall earlier days

indicators.note: the word in places the following pieces inside the word for desert

parts.note: to desert is to forsake
an old copy of The Times is out-of-date reading
an old copy of The Times is out-of-date reading

explanation.surface: Stranded in the desert, someone reads an old newspaper to remember bygone days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like sand but is a verb split around OLD TIMES, and 'In' marks the insertion; the paper is the very one this puzzle appeared in.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something for nostalgia's sake is doing it to recall the past.

clue.text: Gift had teacher worried

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

explanation.surface: A present has left a teacher anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: To gift something is to give it away as a present.

clue.text: Possibly a churchwarden's cask of wine

definitions.meaning: a churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay tobacco ...
a large barrel for wine or port, about 105 gallons

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a smoker's long clay implement and a big wine barrel.

clue.text: Changes involving setting up of secret plant

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: in bell-ringing a peal is a set of changes rung on bells

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: inner, as in inner thoughts, means private or secret

explanation.surface: Alterations include the establishment of a hidden factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up of' gives RENNI; 'Changes' looks like a verb but is the bell-ringer's term, and 'plant' suggests a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant living for more than two years is named by this noun.

clue.text: Liberal academic given employment

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
use, the putting of a thing to work, means employment

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat professor is given a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal in the sense of lavish or generous means plentiful.

clue.text: Chaucerian court official operating in hot weather

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: summer is the season of hot weather
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: An official from Chaucer's court is busy during a heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canterbury Tales includes the tale of the ecclesiastical court's officer who summoned offenders.

clue.text: Bigoted opinion ultimately leads to quarrel

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of opinion

parts.note: a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: Narrow-minded views end up causing an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' suggests a row but is the archer's missile.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow-minded people are bigoted, unwilling to accept other views.

clue.text: Fitzgerald's part in backing formal learning

indicators.note: backing says the run is read backwards
part in says the answer is a run of letters lying in the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A singer contributes to supporting formal education.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Fitzgerald's part' as definition, but 'part in' is the hidden-word signal and 'Fitzgerald' alone defines; ALLE, backed, gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The jazz singer Ella Fitzgerald is identified by her surname alone.

clue.text: Single out a faulty description of size

indicators.note: something faulty is defective, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a flawed account of dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'size' suggests dimensions, but it is the glue-like sealant painters use.
explanation.definitionFit: Size is a thin glue or jelly, so jelly-like is an apt adjective for it.

clue.text: Operatic heroine fired by yen for conformism

parts.note: Norma is the heroine of Bellini's opera
lit means set on fire
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An opera heroine is fired up by a yearning to fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: Conforming to the usual standard is being normal.

clue.text: In which brothers are bound to be poor

definitions.text: In which brothers are bound to be poor

parts.words: In which brothers are bound to be poor
parts.note: the brothers are monks, bound by a vow of poverty in their religious house

explanation.definitionFit: Monks living in a religious house take vows, including one of poverty.

clue.text: A rich man's sleazy bars

definitions.meaning: the rich man in Christ's parable of Lazarus is traditionally named so
seedy drinking places are called this

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin for rich man names the parable figure, and the plural noun means seedy bars.

clue.text: Sentimental wife excluded from dance in school — goodness!

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise, like goodness

indicators.note: a letter excluded from a word is removed from it

parts.note: the waltz is a ballroom dance

explanation.surface: A soppy wife is shut out from a school dance, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluded from' leaves ALTZ; 'in' puts it between the school abbreviation and the exclamation, which the surface hides behind a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is excessive sentimentality, so the adjective means mawkish.

clue.text: Swear about broken axle — must get calmer

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to rant is to shout angrily

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver curses a broken axle and needs something to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' gives ELAX, set inside by 'about'; 'calmer' reads as a comparative adjective but is a noun for a sedative.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that relaxes one is a calmer, a tranquillizing agent.

clue.text: Controls no good in periods of monarchic rule

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: reigns are periods of rule by a monarch

explanation.surface: Controls proved useless during royal eras.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the straps used to control a horse, and so control generally.

clue.text: Obliteration of data inevitable after many years

indicators.note: after puts the piece for inevitable following the one for many years

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
sure means certain to happen

explanation.surface: Losing data is bound to happen over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasing recorded data wipes it out, so the noun means obliteration.

clue.text: Honour accepted by diabolical leader leaving deck?

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it
the leader is the first letter, H, which leaves

parts.note: hellish means devilish or diabolical
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A devilish chief, honoured, departs the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader leaving' drops the H of HELLISH; ELLISH then takes in MBE. 'deck' is the verb meaning adorn, not part of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something out is to adorn or decorate it.

clue.text: Old prison mother will certainly visit, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the words are heard spoken

parts.note: Ma shall see: Ma for mother, shall for will certainly, see for visit

explanation.surface: Mum will surely come to see someone in the old jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marshalsea was a London debtors' prison, where Dickens's father was held; in a non-rhotic accent it sounds like 'Ma shall see'.
explanation.definitionFit: This historic Southwark jail held debtors until it closed in 1842.

clue.text: Bird put on spit, say

indicators.note: say signals a word heard spoken

parts.note: a skewer is a spit for roasting meat

explanation.surface: A bird is put on a roasting spit.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is a seabird; in a non-rhotic British accent it sounds like the roasting skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a predatory seabird that robs other birds of food.

clue.text: Restraint of noblewoman beginning to root for church

indicators.note: one letter stands for another, replacing it

parts.note: a duchess is a noblewoman

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of root

explanation.surface: A duchess's restraint begins to take root in place of church.
explanation.walkthrough: R (first of 'root') replaces CH in DUCHESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is compulsion or forcible restraint.

clue.text: One may cause panic, finding weapon in a tip

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: to list is to tip or lean over
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: Someone finds a weapon on a rubbish tip and alarms everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a dump but is the verb list, to lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaremonger spreads panic with needless warnings.

clue.text: Sort of light — and jolly British!

definitions.meaning: a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol
jolly, in British usage, is an intensifier meaning extremely

explanation.definitionFit: The flare is named after its inventor, and jolly good in Britain means extremely good.

clue.text: Abscond, displaying prickliness for a short time

parts.note: to abscond is to flee
tingly means prickling, showing a stinging sensation

explanation.surface: Someone runs off in a prickly mood briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening briefly or transiently is done in passing, for a moment.
